requirements.title: A free-form whole statement may carry a preceding label
requirements.source: 6.3.2.6 p1; J3/24-007 PDF page 72, printed page 58, line 29.
requirements.definition: A label is permitted before a statement that is not embedded as part of another statement. In free form this includes a whole statement following a semicolon and a statement spread over several continued physical lines. The permission does not attach a second label to an embedded action statement or waive the canonical label spelling, uniqueness, or permitted-use rules.
requirements.oracle: One positive control labels a declaration, assignments, an enclosing action-IF statement, and END PROGRAM, including a labeled assignment continued across lines. A separate control branches forward to an assignment after a semicolon, so lack of that form does not mask the other label contexts. Defined scalar checks provide finite executable context; they are not full effects of the label permission.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The embedded-statement condition is source-accounted, not turned into a negative under this permission. R1141 and the canonical label owner govern the nested action syntax; this batch neither reallocates those R/C IDs nor claims coverage of all labeled statement classes. The informative digit observation does not need a manufactured executable effect.
requirements.dependencies: 3.130 and 6.3.1 define statements. 6.2.5/R611/C603 retain label spelling and use ownership (PDF 70). 6.3.2.4 and 6.3.2.5 supply free-form layout. R1141/11.1.8.4 (PDF 219) distinguishes the enclosing IF from its action. 4.2 p2(1) supplies syntax admission subject to processor resource qualifications.

requirements.title: A free-form statement contains at most one million source characters
requirements.source: 6.3.2.6 p2; J3/24-007 PDF page 72, printed page 58, line 30.
requirements.definition: The total source-character length of one free-form statement cannot exceed 1000000. This is neither a file-byte limit nor a limit on the resulting value of a character literal. Continuation markers and semicolon terminators are excluded by their defining subclauses; interposed commentary and physical line separators are not statement text. Literal quote delimiters remain part of the statement's source spelling even though they do not belong to the literal value.
requirements.oracle: A deterministic generator emits two byte-preserved assignments of exactly 1000000 and 1000001 source characters. Their only byte difference is one inserted x before the terminal Z of the literal. Both use 250 noncomment source lines, hence 249 continuation lines, with a maximum physical line length of 4004; neither violates the F2023 physical-line rule. Twelve interposed comment lines and a semicolon terminator are excluded. The at-limit control checks every literal character, terminal Z, and one blank of assignment padding. The over-limit compile-only diagnose oracle requires a statement-length-specific message within the reconstructed assignment's declared source span, rather than insisting on only its final line.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The explicit kind SELECTED_INT_KIND(9) is justified by 7.4.3.1 p2: the processor must supply an integer representation with decimal range at least 18. All large length literals, loop bounds, substring indices, and LEN inquiries use the selected kind; the weaker default-integer minimum of range 5 is not enough for the boundary. No optional profile gates this mandatory premise. Positive admission remains subject to the 4.2 p2(1) size/complexity qualification; an observed resource failure is not silently rewritten as a fixture defect. Flang's f2018 fallback cannot independently validate the F2023 length premise. An unrelated source location, whole-program recovery range, physical-line/legacy-continuation limit, character-capacity error, crash or timeout cannot replace the statement-length report. Numeric limit text alone is not an accepted message predicate. No permissive compiler option or broad warning allowance is added.
requirements.dependencies: 3.96/3.130 and 6.3.1 define physical lines and statements. 6.3.2.3 excludes commentary, 6.3.2.4 p1 excludes continuation markers, and 6.3.2.5 p2 excludes semicolon terminators. 7.4.4.3/R724 distinguishes source spelling from literal value. 7.4.3.1 p2/p4 (PDF 80) distinguishes mandatory range 18 support from default range 5. 16.9.181 SELECTED_INT_KIND (PDF 454-455), 16.9.122 LEN (PDF 426), 9.4.1 substrings, and 10.2.1.3 character assignment supply the guarded control. 4.2 p2(5), PDF 46, requires reporting capability, not necessarily fatal rejection.

accounting.rationale: PDF 72, line 29: account for the label permission separately from its whole-statement premise.
Separate finite positive controls include a labeled successor after a free-form semicolon without importing fixed-source restrictions or masking the other label contexts.

The permission concerns a whole statement, not the embedded action of an IF statement. Canonical syntax and label rules remain with their existing owners; no extra reporting obligation is inferred from the permission.
PDF 72, printed 58, note following line 29: the observation about a statement's initial digit explains label recognition. It neither redefines R611 nor creates a separate executable effect.

The pinned source says one million characters, not an older edition's effective statement-size or continuation-line ceiling. Exact logical lengths are independently measured from committed ASCII source bytes.

review_rationale: Independent source-first review and verified integration repairs: doc/source_audits/lexical_batch_005.json. Whole-statement label permission includes the valid free-form semicolon successor. The million-character assignments have independently measured source lengths, selected integer arithmetic and a demonstrated-capacity executing control; the over-limit oracle requires a statement-length report.
